title: Bougatsa: Crisp Filo with Semolina Custard, Icing Sugar and Cinnamon
summary: A crisp filo parcel wrapped around a rich semolina custard, served warm and piled high with icing sugar and cinnamon.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring 900 ml whole milk to the boil in a heavy saucepan.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Lower the heat and whisk in 110 g fine semolina in a thin stream, then add 130 g caster sugar and cook, stirring, for 6-8 min until very thick.

steps.title: Enrich
steps.text: Off the heat beat in 60 g diced butter, then 3 eggs one by one until the custard reaches 71 °C, stir in 1 tsp vanilla, press cling film onto the surface and cool 15 min.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C, brush a 25 cm tin with ghee and layer in half of the 400 g filo, brushing every sheet with ghee and leaving the ends overhanging.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Spread the custard over the filo base and fold the overhanging edges over it.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Cover with the remaining filo sheets, brushing each with ghee and tucking the edges in.

steps.title: Score
steps.text: Mark the top layers into squares without cutting through to the custard.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 45-50 min until deep golden and crisp.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Rest 10-15 min, cut along the scored lines and serve warm, dusted heavily with 3 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp ground cinnamon.

tips: Keep stirring the semolina mixture constantly as it thickens so it doesn't catch on the base of the pan.
Let the custard cool briefly under cling film before it goes into the filo, so the pastry doesn't turn soggy.
Dust generously with icing sugar and cinnamon just before serving, while the pie is still warm.
storage: Best eaten the day it's made; keep any leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and warm briefly before serving.
